focus: Q1 existing skill reuse and Q2 phase 001-scenario-contract
answeredQuestions: Q1: What in the existing sk-create-manual-testing-playbook skill (templates, references, validate-playbook-package.cjs and its tests, the existing Turn | Exact user input chain tables) should the conversation work reuse or improve?
Q2: Should phase 001-scenario-contract (the json conversation block, its closed key set and validator rules) be changed, simplified, split or extended, and is anything missing?

graphEvents.label: Validator export seam is safe to import from the runner
Test harness cannot enforce field-path assertions
Conversation block is scanned by unmasked verdict and evergreen checks
Closed key set has no keystroke verb
No adapter coverage check for declared runtimes

label: The validator already exports validatePackage at line 869 and keeps CLI work behind require.main === module with exitIfValidationOff inside that guard, so a runner importing parseConversationScript cannot boot the CLI or exit when validation is off; the test suite already imports across the same seam, which is the precedent REQ-005 relies on.
promptSyncChecks builds a three-tuple copy array and the Turn 1 chain entry is already present at line 619, so REQ-004 is one added tuple and needs no restructuring.
maskFencedCode is the right exclusion primitive and backtickPathChecks already applies it, so the new block needs the same treatment in the two checks that do not mask.

The test helper expectViolation asserts only that a finding code appears, so 'one failing case per rule' would pass even when a rule blames turns instead of turns[2].questions[0].answer; REQ-003's field-path clause is unenforceable with the current helper.

Adding the conversation block to fixtures/clean-package would mutate the positive baseline that REQ-008 and NFR-R02 compare against, because expectClean asserts a package-wide exit 0 and the suite pins per-label prompt-sync warning counts; a second fixture package keeps clean-package byte-identical.

The Turn | Exact user input chain has no home in the snippet template (section 3 lists Prompt, Commands, Expected, Evidence, Pass/Fail, Failure Triage, Optional Supplemental Checks) and no shipped file contains the header, yet SKILL.md names its Turn 1 as the copy a runner sends, so 001 ships a second multi-turn format beside one nothing exercises and must state which to choose.

validateScenario passes raw file text to verdictChecks and evergreenChecks, neither of which masks fences, so conversation-block JSON is scanned by FORBIDDEN_VERDICTS (PARTIAL, READY, UNAUTOMATABLE, BLOCKED), SKIP_BLOCKER_MISSING, BAKED_RUN_TRANSCRIPT and DEVELOPER_ABSOLUTE_PATH; a check command containing BLOCKED becomes a validation error on an otherwise valid file.

ADR-001 and 001 spec section 2 claim a table cell cannot carry a regular expression with a pipe, but splitTableRow splits on (?<!\\)\| and promptValue turns \| back into |, so an escaped pipe survives one cell; the decision still holds on label lists, backtick stripping and per-turn shell checks, so the justification should rest on those.

The closed key set has no keystroke verb: send is one line of text and action is restart or compact, so a script cannot press Escape, Ctrl-C, an arrow key or a bare Enter, while every fresh scratch project shows an onboarding or trust selector on first launch; an empty send is neither required nor rejected, so Enter-only is expressible only by accident.

answer.select overloads array length into a mode bit: two or more labels mean multi-select, but a runner cannot distinguish that from a single-select dialog toggled twice and the validator cannot check which the runtime offers; a separate multi field removes the ambiguity.
runtimes is top-level only, so one script across five runtimes cannot carry a turn that applies to one runtime; a Codex-only tool-question turn is today a second whole script.
optional only relaxes a required question; nothing can assert a question must not be asked and nothing counts asks, so an answer-once regression in the first consumer is unrepresentable.

timeout_ms accepts 0 (non-negative), which is an instant failure and almost certainly a typo, and the block contract states that a failing setup command stops the run but says nothing about a failing check, leaving evidence-volume policy to phase 002.

Nothing binds a declared runtime id to a shipped adapter: 001 exports five ids while 002 may ship partial tool-question support for one of them, so a script can validate clean and be unrunnable; a 002 test iterating CONVERSATION_RUNTIMES and asserting one adapter entry per id closes it.
